analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/operations/provider-release.md (lines 1033-1040 on head, plus a date bump) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (new `darkbloom update --rollback` and `--yes` flags, plus the quarantine wording). No executable code, configuration or enforcement changed, so no control was weakened by this diff.

The documented rollback behavior is relevant to T-043 (watchdog rollback authority) and T-034/T-054 (build qualification). The docs say the rollback is a local operation that contacts no coordinator. It restores the retained predecessor only after its hash and signature checks pass. It quarantines the bad release and refuses when the installed app does not match the recorded release, when another update or recovery holds the lease, or when the Mac is part of a cluster pair. This is consistent with existing guards: it needs a local operator, hash/signature verification, and the update lease. The docs also state that rollback does not extend App Attest authorization. The serving gates (A-016/A-017, T-053/T-054) remain platform-owned, so a rolled-back older build would still need current qualification to serve. The docs say runtime policy must retain needed older official builds during adoption.

The actual implementation (UpdateRollback.swift, SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift) is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the code enforces the documented checks: the downgrade being limited to the retained predecessor, signature verification, the quarantine, and the `--yes` requirement for non-TTY stdin. A later pass that sees the Swift rollback code should confirm those checks, and that rolling back cannot reinstall a revoked or unqualified build. The cli-reference patch excerpt is truncated, but the base text and visible hunks show only documentation. The threat model may need a note on user-initiated rollback as a downgrade path in T-043/T-047 once the code is reviewed. No concrete regression is established from this documentation-only diff.
